stories.headline: Government weighs 22-cargo LNG plan for winter supply
stories.summary: Pakistan's government was considering a Petroleum Division proposal to import 22 LNG cargoes, estimated at about $2 billion, to manage winter gas demand. The Cabinet Committee on Energy had not yet taken up the summary, so the imports were not an approved transaction at publication time.
stories.what_happened: The Petroleum Division sought authorisation for 22 LNG cargoes for winter supply, with some cargoes expected to be sourced from the United States and Azerbaijan. The Cabinet Committee on Energy had not yet considered the summary.
stories.why_it_matters: The decision links winter energy security, industrial gas supply, foreign-exchange costs and Pakistan's external energy dependence.
stories.pakistan_perspective: The proposal should be described as pending, not approved. Delays could affect gas allocation to industry, power, fertiliser, CNG and cement while residential demand rises.
key_takeaways: The Petroleum Division proposed importing 22 LNG cargoes for winter demand.
The estimated import cost was about $2 billion.
The CCOE had not yet taken up the summary.
facts: Pakistan's Petroleum Division proposed 22 LNG cargoes for winter 2026 supply, with an estimated cost of about $2 billion.

stories.headline: Kremlin says Russia is willing in principle to resume Ukraine talks in November
stories.summary: Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said President Vladimir Putin told US special envoy Steve Witkoff that Russia was willing in principle to resume talks with Ukraine and the United States in November. No such talks had taken place since February.
stories.what_happened: Putin met Witkoff in St Petersburg and, according to Ushakov, signalled willingness in principle for a new round of talks next month focused on a post-conflict security system for Russia and Ukraine.
stories.why_it_matters: A return to trilateral diplomacy would be a significant change after months without such talks, though willingness to negotiate is not the same as a ceasefire or settlement.
key_takeaways: Russia signalled willingness in principle to resume talks in November.
The proposed format involves Russia, Ukraine and the United States.
The previous such talks were in February.
facts: Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said Russia was willing in principle to resume talks with Ukraine and the United States in November 2026.

stories.headline: France's 10-year bond yield reaches 5%, highest since 2002
stories.summary: France's benchmark 10-year government bond yield touched 5.002%, its highest level since 2002, as investors focused on fiscal weakness, political uncertainty and rising global borrowing costs.
stories.what_happened: The 10-year French yield crossed 5%, while the spread over benchmark German Bunds was around 157 basis points.
stories.why_it_matters: The move illustrates how fiscal credibility and political uncertainty can raise sovereign borrowing costs even in advanced economies.
key_takeaways: It was the highest level since 2002.
The France-Germany 10-year spread was around 157 basis points.
facts: France's 10-year government bond yield reached 5% in October 2026, its highest level since 2002.

stories.headline: IMF urges India to use exchange-rate flexibility as first line of defence
stories.summary: IMF Asia and Pacific Department director Krishna Srinivasan said India should allow the dollar-rupee exchange rate to move as a first line of defence against the oil shock, arguing that foreign-exchange intervention has limited benefits beyond the near term.
stories.what_happened: The IMF advice came as the Reserve Bank of India used dollar sales and other measures to support the rupee after it approached record lows.
stories.why_it_matters: The episode highlights the policy trade-off between using reserves to defend a currency and allowing exchange-rate adjustment to absorb external shocks.
key_takeaways: Krishna Srinivasan leads the IMF's Asia and Pacific Department.
He described exchange-rate movement as a first line of defence against shocks.
The RBI had intervened to support the rupee.
facts: IMF Asia-Pacific director Krishna Srinivasan advised India to let the exchange rate act as the first line of defence against the oil shock.
